title: While the Stars Unnumbered Roll
description: While the Stars Unnumbered Roll in Tonic Solfa to ST. BEES, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 555, “Night”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BEES; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: While the stars un-num-bered roll Round the ev-er con-stant pole, Far a-bove these span-gled skies All my thoughts to God shall rise.

lines: All my thoughts to God shall rise.
From on high He shall impart
On the wings of faith and love.
What if death my sleep invade; —
Should I be of death afraid?
Death may strike, but cannot harm.
Waits to waft my soul on high!
Death is life, and labor, rest;
Welcome sleep or death to me,
Still secure, for still with Thee!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ST. BEES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
